observances.name: Shravan Purnima Vrat (Satyanarayan Vrat)
observances.description: Full-moon fasting day of Shravan month; Satyanarayan Puja is commonly performed.

observances.name: Raksha Bandhan
observances.description: Festival celebrating the bond between brothers and sisters, marked by tying a rakhi thread; falls on Shravan Purnima.

observances.name: Heramba Sankashti Chaturthi
observances.description: Monthly fast for Lord Ganesha observed on the fourth day after the full moon.

observances.name: Krishna Janmashtami
observances.description: Birth anniversary of Lord Krishna, observed with a day-long fast broken at midnight, followed by Dahi Handi celebrations.

observances.name: Aja Ekadashi
observances.description: Krishna Paksha Ekadashi of Bhadrapada month, observed with a fast for Lord Vishnu.

observances.name: Bhaum Pradosh Vrat
observances.description: Twilight fast for Lord Shiva, falling on a Tuesday this cycle.

observances.name: Masik Shivaratri
observances.description: Monthly night-vigil fast for Lord Shiva.

observances.name: Pithori Amavasya
observances.description: New-moon day of Bhadrapada month, observed by mothers for their children's wellbeing. Sources disagree slightly on whether this falls on Sept 10 or Sept 11 local time — shown here as Sept 10.

observances.name: Hartalika Teej
observances.description: Fast observed by married women for marital wellbeing, ahead of Ganesh Chaturthi.

observances.name: Ganesh Chaturthi
observances.description: Festival marking the birth of Lord Ganesha; the start of a multi-day Ganesh Utsav.

observances.name: Radha Ashtami
observances.description: Birth anniversary of Radha, celebrated with temple decorations and bhajans.

observances.name: Parsva Ekadashi (Parivartini Ekadashi)
observances.description: Shukla Paksha Ekadashi of Bhadrapada month, also known as Parivartini or Vamana Ekadashi.

observances.name: Guru Pradosh Vrat
observances.description: Twilight fast for Lord Shiva, falling on a Thursday this cycle.

observances.name: Anant Chaturdashi (Ganesh Visarjan)
observances.description: Closing day of Ganesh Utsav, marked by the immersion (visarjan) of Ganesha idols; also a fast for Lord Vishnu's Ananta form.
